# Constant and mixed trigonal norm obstructions

Version3,3October2026. The constant-norm criterion retains its focused
independent audit; the fixed-X mixed-norm exclusion reuses the exact
geometric unit-ideal certificate checked on25September2026. The
two-torsion uniqueness assertion is a Riemann--Roch consequence.

Let F in F25[x] be squarefree of degree10 and let X be the smooth
projective model of y^3=F. Suppose the Frobenius25 polynomial of J(X)
reduces modulo2 to an irreducible degree18 polynomial whose roots have
multiplicative order N, with Euler phi(N)>18. Then there are no rational
functions P,R in bar(F5)(x) satisfying

                            P^3+F=R^2.

For the fixed genus-nine X, the established polynomial has N=171 and
phi(N)=108. Consequently no bounded Kummer norm solution

                         P^3+FQ^3=R^2

has nonzero constant Q. All three Qdegree0 pole charts are therefore
excluded at once, including the open Pdegree6 and Pdegree4 charts.
The exclusion is over the full algebraic closure and does not depend
on a multiplier ansatz, coefficient-field search or newly computed
sixth-root zeta polynomial.

For this fixed \(X\), let \(O\) be its unique point at infinity.
Every nonzero \(L\in J(X)[2]\) satisfies
\[
h^0(L(7O))=0,\qquad h^0(L(8O))\le1,\qquad h^0(L(9O))=1.
\]
Hence \(L\) has a unique effective degree-nine representative \(D\).
The Kummer function with divisor \(2D-18O\) is unique up to scalar.
This concerns actual geometric representatives; it does not assert
reducedness of a polynomial norm scheme.

The mechanism uses the actual curve D:z^6=F. Its primitive-sixth
Jacobian factor has the same Frobenius polynomial modulo2 as J(X),
by equality of all unramified Euler factors and of the omitted local
factors. A norm solution gives an actual nonconstant primitive-sixth
map D->E:v^2=u^3+1. Since Frobenius25 on E is -5, the binary order
contradicts the degree of its required root-of-unity Weil eigenvalue.

For the same fixed polynomial \(F\), there are also no polynomials
\(g,H,J\in\overline{\mathbf F}_5[x]\) satisfying
\[
F+g^3=H^2J^3,\qquad \deg g\le3,\quad H,J\text{ monic of degree two}.
\]
This is an unconditional geometric assertion: repeated roots and common
roots of \(H,J\) are included. It uses the full coefficient ideal, with
no support, trace, cover, squarefreeness or nonvanishing assumptions.
In particular \(F+g^3=(x-r)^4C_2^3\) is impossible for every geometric
\(r\) and every monic quadratic \(C_2\), by taking \(H=(x-r)^2\).

For nonconstant Q, the fixed-X carriers and their backup-factor tests
are handled by the [complete sieve](backup_double_cover_exclusion.md).

[Proof](../../../Proofs/jacobians/isogeny_sieves/trigonal_constant_norm_obstruction.md) · [Binary check](../../../scripts/arithmetic/check_degree2_frobenius_orbits.py).

# Weak cyclic two-branch curves constrain every irreducible reflection module

Version1,3 October2026. Whole scoped PASS in the [independent audit](../../../Research/audits/WEAK_CYCLIC_REFLECTION_MODULE_CONSTRAINTS_AUDIT_2026_10_03.md). The reflection eigenspace hypothesis is essential and is not supplied by arbitrary higher-rank spin or trace modules.

Let k be algebraically closed of odd characteristic p, and let a finite group G act faithfully on a smooth connected projective curve Z with Z/G=P¹ and exactly TWO branch values: cyclic Cp of lower break ONE and cyclic C2. Let V be an irreducible projective G-module of dimension n≥TWO on which the original tame involution has eigenspace dimensions ONE and n−ONE. The representation need not be faithful.

Then n≤p. The prescribed cyclic lift supplies a generating opposite-class tuple a,b,c; its normalized unipotent matrices A,B are regular Jn blocks. Writing the repeated eigenvalue of AB as ρ gives ρ^n=−ONE. This irreducible matrix tuple is linearly rigid and is realizable over the smallest finite field F_q containing ρ. Its entire projective image lies in PSL_n(F_q).

If n is EVEN, inverse conjugacy imposes
\[
4\mid\frac{q-1}{\gcd(n,q-1)},
\qquad\text{equivalently}\qquad
v_2(q-1)\ge v_2(n)+2.
\]
The stronger-looking condition 4n|(q−ONE) is equivalent only when n|(q−ONE); that divisibility is not automatic because ρ can lose odd factors in its order.

In characteristicFIVE the only possible dimensions are THREE andFIVE: dimensions TWO andFOUR violate the displayed condition. For n=THREE, ρ=−ONE gives a realization over F5 with an invariant nondegenerate symmetric form; either primitive-SIXTH-root value of ρ gives a realization over F25 with an invariant nondegenerate F5-Hermitian form. For n=FIVE, ρ=−ONE is forced, and the realization is over F5 with an invariant nondegenerate symmetric form. Thus odd dimension does NOT uniformly imply prime-field realization or symmetric self-duality.

No rank bound for arbitrary modules, finite coefficient extraction, actual X-atlas or unmarked common-cover exclusion follows. Both actual source maps must still be retained in any application.

# An odd equivariant rational map excludes a fourth-order line obstruction

Version1,3 October2026. [Root whole-scope review PASS](../../Research/audits/RANK_THREE_SCALAR_TARGET_AND_TAME_IDENTITY_AUDIT_2026_10_03.md).

Let A be a finite group acting on a smooth projective connected curve D over an algebraically closed field. Let M be an A-invariant line class with scalar linearization obstruction α∈H²(A,k×). Let f:D→P¹ be an ACTUAL finite A-equivariant map of degree a, with any action of A on P¹; that action may have a kernel. Then
\[
\boxed{2a\alpha=0.}
\]
In particular, if a is ODD, the TWO-primary component of α cannot have order at leastFOUR. The assertion allows inseparable maps: it concerns the actual finite flat norm, not a chosen separable completion.

Consequently a curve carrying an invariant line whose obstruction pulls back to orderFOUR orEIGHT on its original acting group has no equivariant odd-degree rational pencil. This conclusion uses the ORIGINAL group and obstruction; replacing it by an effective target quotient does not remove the pullback obstruction.

This does not assert that every curve admits such a pencil, classify its finite group, or produce a second étale endpoint map.
